utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everybody in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good afternoon to everyone. May we have the appearances, please, before we go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm happy to see that the Registrar wants a even longer day, as he's been wishing everybody good morning. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, Charlotte Frew, and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, Ms. Tatjana Savic, Mr. Brian Jacobi, Ms. Ivana Batista, and Ms. Wangeci Wahome appearing for Stanisic Defence. We have our interns here who are leaving, so we -- we thought that it would be appropriate that they spend one day inside the room. Thank you very much for your understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic, Igor Pantelic, Aleksandar Aleksic, and Ms. Katarina Danicic appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any -- Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Jelena Nikolic, lawyer, representing the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm going to ask to go into private session immediately, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I was actually going to take that appearance in closed session, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Private session will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Private, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, we were just wondering --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, we should be in private session still.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we conducted the interview of two coming witnesses scheduled for -- for this week. It's ST-195 and ST -- I believe, 197, if I'm not mistaken. No. ST-128. So those are the witnesses which are coming after the witness today. During the -- during the interview, these witnesses brought our attention to the fact that one of them, namely ST-195, has testified in an another case in Bosnia-Herzegovina -- before the state court of Bosnia-Herzegovina concerning the subject matter of his testimony over here. So -- and that -- that transcript or any kind of knowledge was -- was -- we were deprived of -- of knowledge about that. We received the documents of his testimony in one of the cases, so apparently there are two cases which are -- are currently tried before the court of Bosnia and Herzegovina for -- concerning the same incident that these -- all three of these witnesses are -- are going to testify about. Now, we believe that -- that we should have been disclosed this testimony in his case, like we were disclosed the previous one, and we ask the office of the prosecutor to provide that. Concerning the Witness ST-128, is a more or less similar situation. He gave the statement to the prosecution -- to the prosecutor's office of the state court of Bosnia-Herzegovina concerning the same incident in -- in the spring of this year. So we requested the office of the prosecutor to provide us with that document also, because we -- we believe that we should be disclosed all the relevant documents concerning their prior testimonies, their statement given to the officials in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Now, honestly, Your Honours, the Defence was not aware of the fact that there was a second case tried before the court of Bosnia and Herzegovina at all concerning this same incident. So we are aware of one of the cases, and we're not aware of the second case. And in all -- in all understanding of the difficulties, we believe that we should be made available the relevant documents, because these documents definitely are -- are concerning the -- directly with the subject matter that we are going to hear from the witnesses that are coming this week. And I raised that issue with -- with my friend Ms. Korner from the Prosecution, and we decided that -- that there was -- since the time is so short between our finding out about these things and informing the -- the Office of the Prosecution and the start of the proceedings today that we raise it in court and ask for your Judges' opinion or instructions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I assume, Mr. Zecevic, that there is no dispute as to the disclosure insofar as possible from the calling side in this matter, but the -- and at 15 years on in the life of this Tribunal there is an established protocol as to the mechanics as to how this is achieved when we're dealing with transcripts from Tribunals other than this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, Your Honour, there isn't. First of all, we didn't know any more than the Defence did that either of these two witnesses had testified in the state court or had made a statement and one had testified. Both occasions happened after we had interviewed them. There are no transcripts. We're not in possession of anything that we could have disclosed even if we had known about it. They don't produce transcripts at the state court unless specifically requested. So we are in no position to disclose anything that we don't have. We can, if we're asked to, make the request that the testimony -- well, the statement we can certainly probably get very quickly, but the testimony would have to be transcribed. But as I say, we strongly reject any suggestion that we're under any obligation to disclose matters that we don't have and don't know anything about. As a matter of courtesy, we'll see what we can do to arrange it, because I know that it's easier for us than it is for the Defence, but the Defence have exactly the same access to the BiH court and the BiH court regards as we do. One of the difficulties, of course, is it obviously never occurred to either witness that it was relevant to tell us this in advance, and the state court don't tell us because they don't know who our witnesses are. So that's the upshot. But the upshot is this: Effectively, we will assist the Defence to get these documents. We cannot, however, do it before the witnesses testify, and possibly we might -- if -- if -- the witness who made a statement, we may be able to get hold of that quicker, but not the person who testified. So where -- the suggestion we make is that the witnesses go ahead, are cross-examined in the normal way, and then if anything turns up after the testimony, if necessary the witness can be recalled. So that's the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. I didn't mean to suggest that there was any obligation on the part of the Prosecution to do the impossible. It's just that as a matter of professional courtesy the -- one would expect that you -- insofar as you're able to assist, that you would. And I think that would go -- that goes without saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Absolutely. And if we know in advance about testimonies, we do get them. I mean -- but, as I say, it's more of a courtesy than anything else. Because, as I say, it's got not much to do with us. But this time we didn't know; it came as as much a surprise to us as to Mr. Zecevic that this has happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may be of assistance, we don't need the transcripts, we just need the audiotapes. And according to my knowledge, all audiotapes exist. And I would strongly disagree with my learned friend about the ability of Defence and the ability of the Office of the Prosecutor of this court in relation to the state court of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I don't want to comment on that. On paper it does appear to be similar, but in practice it is not. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we take the adjournment now to --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, as it's quarter to 3.00, 4.15. I'm sorry, would Your Honours say 4.15? I'd like an hour and a half, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Very well. --- Break taken at 2.48 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, thank you very much for the time that you allowed us. We could go almost immediately into closed session and there are a few matters to deal with before the witness comes in, but they need to be dealt with in closed session. But can I just say that we've made inquiries in respect of Mr. Zecevic's request. Almost certainly we'll be able to get the statement that was made here tomorrow, and it there's a possibility even that we may be able to get the -- the tapes, yes. So, Your Honours, can we go into closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before we do that, I'm wondering whether -- and this may be something -- I don't know if it's for closed session, but as -- I'm looking -- I'm reminding myself of the OTP's e-mail of Friday in terms of the schedule for this week, and I'm wondering whether, having regard to the delay today, I should make inquiries of the Registry at an early stage as to the possibility of an extended sitting tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'd be very grateful. Thank you very much, Your Honour, if that could happen, because, as I explained, for various reasons, and they're professional reasons, I can't be here on Wednesday. So -- we still hope to finish. My understanding is that Mr. Krgovic will take a couple of sessions, but that Mr. Cvijetic will be shorter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Could either side indicate as to how much time the Registry should be looking for tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I would have thought at the -- a maximum of one extra session, at the absolute maximum, and hopefully we can still complete within the allowed time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic seems to be in agreement with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can confirm that because I discussed with my learned friend from the Prosecutor. So I think we're down for maybe one additional session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the Registry would make the appropriate inquiries, and we would report to let counsel know tomorrow where we are. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we now go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 31st day of August, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.04 p.m.,
